assertions.name: C4_the_exact_Sturm_real_root_count_DISCRIMINATES
assertions.source: hand-built cases [('x**2 + 1', 0), ('x**2 - 1', 2), ('x**3 - 2', 1), ('x**4 - 1', 2)] match the known answers; this is exact root COUNTING (Sturm sequences), not a numerical root-find, so no float64 enters and a borderline field cannot be miscounted

assertions.name: C1_the_embedding_count_CLOSES
assertions.source: r_1 + 2*r_2 = deg for every field — a real embedding plus a conjugate pair account for every embedding, with none left over

assertions.name: C2_the_degree_REPRODUCES_the_companion_probe_s_C_irr
assertions.source: the companion probe got C_irr by summing Galois-ORBIT degrees off the Magma fixtures; this reads the minimal polynomial's DEGREE. Two routes, same six numbers — so neither is a parsing artifact

assertions.name: C3_every_minimal_polynomial_is_IRREDUCIBLE_over_Q
assertions.source: otherwise 'the trace field' is not a field and counting its embeddings would be meaningless

assertions.name: FIVE_of_six_trace_fields_are_TOTALLY_IMAGINARY
assertions.source: totally imaginary ['4_1', 'm135', 's000', 't00000', 'v0000']; the only field with a real embedding is ['5_2']. So on this sample the mirror acts FREELY on the node set almost everywhere, and 5_2 is the exception

assertions.name: 5_2_s_fixed_node_is_FORCED_BY_PARITY_not_a_coincidence
assertions.source: 5_2 is the only odd-degree field (3), and no involution acts freely on a set of odd size — so a mirror-fixed node is unavoidable there, while 4_1's two nodes can be freely swapped. This is parity, not a property of the particular polynomial

assertions.name: RECORDED_NEGATIVE_this_is_NOT_an_escape_from_the_mirror_exclusion
assertions.source: I first read the fixed point as evading QuiverMirrorAutomorphismExcluded, on the theory that it excludes a FREELY acting mirror. Reading the theorem first: its hypothesis is hσ : ∀ e, Ω (σ e) = Ω e — count-invariance, which says nothing about freeness. A σ with fixed points can satisfy it and is excluded identically. The parity fact survives; the consequence I nearly drew from it does not

assertions.name: WHAT_THIS_IS_an_INPUT_to_the_arrow_question
assertions.source: the measured (r_1, r_2) is the bar grading any bar-graded quiver on these nodes must reproduce. It does not produce arrows, a potential, or A_omega, and no construction is proposed here

description: qou-q9ih D1-b, arrow question. The companion probe closed the NODE count as arithmetic (single Galois orbit, C_irr = [trace field : Q]). Arrows in a bar-graded quiver need the bar grading of the node set, and the single-orbit result says where to read it: nodes are the embeddings of the trace field, complex conjugation acts on them, and a rep is self-conjugate exactly when its embedding is real. So the grading is r_1 mirror-FIXED nodes plus r_2 swapped pairs. Measured exactly by Sturm sequences: five of six trace fields are TOTALLY IMAGINARY; 5_2 is the only one with a real embedding and cannot avoid one, because its trace field has ODD degree and no involution acts freely on an odd-size set. RECORDED NEGATIVE: I first read this as an escape from QuiverMirrorAutomorphismExcluded -- that the theorem excludes a freely-acting mirror and a fixed point evades it. Reading the theorem shows that is WRONG: its hypothesis is count-invariance (Omega(sigma e) = Omega e), which says nothing about freeness, so a fixed point is no escape. The parity fact stands; the consequence does not. What this gives is the measured (r_1, r_2) any bar-graded construction must reproduce -- an INPUT to the arrow question, not an answer. Scope-(a); four of six are census manifolds, valid for the grading and not automatically valid as D1-b nodes. Nothing wired; no fit; A_omega underived.

recorded_negative.claim_i_nearly_made: a mirror with a fixed point escapes QuiverMirrorAutomorphismExcluded because that theorem excludes a freely-acting mirror
recorded_negative.why_it_is_wrong: the theorem's hypothesis is count-invariance (hσ : ∀ e, Ω (σ e) = Ω e), not freeness; a σ with fixed points satisfies it just as well and is excluded on the same terms
recorded_negative.how_it_was_caught: read the Lean statement before writing the claim
